messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock the priority heatmap for the next cycle. We're resource-constrained; want to pick the highest ROI slices: batching pilot, adaptive prefix caching, quantization recommendations, or eval-triggered alerts. Thoughts?
Sam (Eng): Heatmap idea is good. My priority order is: 1) adaptive caching (low infra risk), 2) batching heuristics (medium), 3) quant recs (high ML effort), 4) eval alerts (depends on eval infra).
Liam (ML): Agree w/ Sam but emphasize we can prototype quant recs with offline scoring first — gives signal without infra work. Also caching has the best immediate token $ savings if we can target common prefixes.
Anika (Design): Will need a tiny UI surface for recs + an admin toggle for pilots. For eval-alerts, we should design a simple alert card: "What changed" + examples. Keep it opt-in.
Ravi (CS): From customers: 3 asks in priority order — better latency for interactive features, lower per-token cost for high-volume jobs, and proactive regression alerts. So batching helps latency/cost, caching helps cost/latency, quant helps cost but customers worry about quality.
Sam (Eng): Tradeoffs: batching = throughput gains but adds tail latency complexity; caching = fast wins if prefix hit rate > ~15%; quantization = engineering + model validation effort. We should estimate eng-weeks per initiative.
Maya (PM): Proposal: run two small pilots in parallel: (A) adaptive caching + small UI toggle, (B) offline quant recs prototype + eval set. Keep batching as follow-up depending on pilot lift. Eval-alerts as stretch if pilot infra is ready.
Liam (ML): For (B) I can produce baseline ranking logic in 2 weeks. Need labeled dev set for quality thresholds. Can we get existing eval buckets?
Ravi (CS): I can pull 4 customer prompts sets (prod anonymized) — will share as soon as legal OKs.
Anika (Design): UI mock for caching toggle + recs card — I can ship a clickable prototype by EOW. Keep it minimal: rec name, expected savings, opt-in toggle.
Sam (Eng): Rough eng estimate: caching pilot ~3 wks (1 eng + infra part-time), quant recs offline ~2 wks (ML + small infra), batching pilot ~4-6 wks (more infra changes).
Maya (PM): Acceptance criteria draft (we'll refine):
- Caching pilot: prefix hit rate >= 15% on pilot traffic OR end-to-end token cost reduction >= 8% for pilot cohort
- Latency: p50 gen latency change <= +15ms, p95 <= +35ms (non-regressive)
- Quant recs (offline): precision >= 0.7 on recommended-safe set, suggested quant configs reduce token cost by >= 10% in sim
- Eval-alerts: precision >= 0.75 and actionable example diffs in 80% of alerts
Liam (ML): Those look reasonable. For quant precision target, suggest we also track harm-rate (how often output quality degrades per prompt type).
Sam (Eng): Also add rollout gate: canary to 5% traffic, monitor token cost and failure/error rate for 48h before wider rollout.
Ravi (CS): Customer comms note: be explicit about quality tradeoffs for quantization recs. Offer a "compare" mode in console showing before/after for a few examples.
Anika (Design): I'll design the compare UI pattern. Good call.
Maya (PM): Next steps: Sam to validate infra estimate by EOD Tuesday; Liam to confirm labeling needs; Ravi to start vendor/customer prompt pull; Anika to drop mocks; I'll assemble a one-pager for leadership with heatmap + ask for 2 FTEs for 6 weeks.
Sam (Eng): ack. I'll add a short risk list: cache invalidation, KV storage sizing, and prefix matching correctness.
ops-bot: CI pipeline: small-infra-branch passed 14/14 checks. :white_check_mark:
Maya (PM): Perfect — let's reconvene Friday 11am to finalize scope. If anyone needs to reprioritize, ping here. :calendar:
Sam (Eng): Thanks — will post updated eng-week estimates in thread.
Liam (ML): I'll attach a quick eval sketch before Friday.
Ravi (CS): Will coordinate legal for data share, ETA Thu.
Anika (Design): Dropping initial mock link: https://figma.placeholder/opt-tools-mock (private)
Maya (PM): Awesome — closing for now. :rocket:
